question: Can black-box response distributions reveal whether an LLM tracks a user's latent intent rather than incidental prompt wording, and how does that behavior vary across model family, size, and domain?

key_findings.claim: The framework defines intent comprehension behaviorally as invariance within evaluator-defined intent classes plus separation across different intents.
key_findings.evidence: Exact IC requires equal full response distributions for equivalent prompts and unequal distributions for different intents. Sufficient and epsilon-sufficient variants map responses through an evaluator and permit distributional distance tolerance, making the definition usable for numeric, categorical, embedded, or scored outputs.

key_findings.claim: A nested variance decomposition separates variation associated with intent, paraphrase, and repeated sampling, but those labels are interpretations of experimental factors rather than identified cognitive causes.
key_findings.evidence: Intent Sensitivity is between-intent variance, Articulation Sensitivity is between-paraphrase variance nested within intent, and Model Uncertainty is within-cell residual variance; the normalized shares sum to one. A mixed-effects REML estimator with hierarchical bootstrap reduces small-cell bias. Residual variance can combine sampling randomness, epistemic uncertainty, aleatoric task variation, and extraction noise.

anchors.section: F Estimating Variance Decomposition via ANOVA

key_findings.claim: Larger tested models generally place more response variation on intent and score higher on the combined index, but size is neither monotone nor separable from family and training design.
key_findings.evidence: Across five models, the small LLaMA models attribute about 20% of variation to intent while larger models are near 50%; Gemma 12B is comparable to or better than some larger systems. Larger models also show greater articulation sensitivity, rankings change by domain, and the authors explicitly describe the size association rather than a scaling law.

key_findings.claim: The automated paraphrase and extraction pipeline is substantially but not perfectly validated, leaving residual intent drift as measurement error.
key_findings.evidence: Two annotators judge 95% and 91% of 200 paraphrases intent-preserving and agree on 89%; they judge 94% and 91% of numeric extractions correct and agree on 93%. The paraphrase kappa is only about 0.16 under severe class imbalance and the authors note that the check validates preservation, not surface diversity.

method.core_idea: Hold latent intent fixed while varying articulation, vary intent within a common task structure, and attribute the resulting response-distribution variation to those nested experimental factors.
method.mechanism: GPT-4.1 creates structured quantitative intents and cross-lingual paraphrases, filters semantic drift, and selects diverse wording. Five open models generate repeated responses at fixed temperature; numeric values are extracted and standardized. A nested random-effects model estimates intent, paraphrase, and residual variance shares, then ICI harmonically combines intent coverage with the fraction of systematic variation attributable to intent.
assumptions: The evaluator's intent labels and response-value map capture what users actually mean and care about.
Retained paraphrases change wording without materially changing intent, framing, or implied assumptions.
Nested additive variance components are a useful summary of the response distributions.
Repeated temperature-one samples and the same prompt set permit meaningful relative model comparisons.

techniques.role: Creates within-intent wording changes and between-intent semantic changes as separate experimental factors.
Estimates Intent Sensitivity, Articulation Sensitivity, and residual Model Uncertainty.
Combines high between-intent separation and low relative articulation dependence in one score.
Induces large surface-form variation while attempting to preserve meaning.
Propagates uncertainty while respecting task, prompt, and repeated-response nesting.

evaluations.setting: Twenty-four quantitative guesstimation tasks in five domains, 12 intents and 10 paraphrases per task, with 25 requested samples per cell.
evaluations.metric: IS, AS, MU, Meaningful Variability Share, and ICI from about 1.77 million valid responses.
evaluations.result: LLaMA 3B/8B have high residual uncertainty and low intent sensitivity; Gemma 12B/27B and LLaMA 70B show higher intent shares, modestly different ICI, and more articulation sensitivity.
evaluations.baseline: Cross-model descriptive comparison under the same prompts and temperature.

evaluations.setting: Domain-stratified comparison across transportation, finance, health/nutrition, logistics, and social planning.
evaluations.result: No model dominates all domains; LLaMA 70B leads selected health/transport intent sensitivity while Gemma 27B leads logistics, finance, and social planning in the reported plots.
evaluations.baseline: Aggregate model ranking across all tasks.

evaluations.setting: Human audit of 200 paraphrases and 200 numeric extractions with two annotators.
evaluations.metric: Per-annotator acceptance, raw agreement, and Cohen's kappa.
evaluations.result: Intent preservation is labeled 95%/91% with 89% agreement; extraction correctness is 94%/91% with 93% agreement.
evaluations.baseline: Automated GPT filtering and numerical extraction without human checks.

evaluations.setting: Robustness analyses over 5-25 responses per cell, Gaussian/Laplace/Student-t residual families, and lower sampling temperatures.
evaluations.metric: Average variance shares and qualitative model ordering.
evaluations.result: Draw-count and distribution-family changes leave the main decomposition pattern broadly similar; lower temperature reduces residual uncertainty but does not remove the intent/articulation tradeoff.
evaluations.baseline: Twenty-five samples, Gaussian mixed effects, and temperature one.

limitations: Author-stated: the empirical benchmark covers quantitative guesstimation, two model families, and five domains rather than intent in general.
Author-stated: only first and second moments are used in the main decomposition, and qualitative evaluator mappings can be subjective.
Author-stated: cross-lingual paraphrases can drift in framing or granularity despite filtering.
Reviewer inference: consistent response distributions can be coherently wrong, reward-hacked to the evaluator, or insensitive because the model ignores both intent and wording.
failure_modes: Low output variance can make normalized shares and ICI unstable or falsely flattering on deterministic/ignored tasks.
If paraphrases encode dialect or pragmatic cues that legitimately affect a response, AS can misclassify useful adaptation as brittleness.
An evaluator that collapses semantically distinct responses to one value can hide failures in the unmeasured response dimensions.
Model family, post-training, tokenizer, and size are confounded, so an apparent parameter trend can reverse outside the tested models.
reusable_insights: Robustness needs two-sided testing: invariance to meaning-preserving changes and sensitivity to minimal meaning-changing interventions.
Repeated-sample evaluation can distinguish prompt dependence from sampling uncertainty that a single answer conceals.
Accuracy and intent robustness are orthogonal audit axes; a deployment needs both.
Use nested estimators and resampling when prompt cells have unequal or sparse valid generations.
open_questions: Does ICI predict real user satisfaction, correction frequency, safety, or task return better than accuracy and prompt-sensitivity metrics?
How should legitimate pragmatic adaptation, personalization, and ambiguity be separated from unwanted articulation sensitivity?
Can adversarial human-authored paraphrases and multi-turn intent clarification invalidate rankings from synthetic single-turn prompts?
What training interventions reduce AS without suppressing sensitivity to genuine intent changes?

competitive_landscape.title: ProSA: Assessing and Understanding the Prompt Sensitivity of LLMs
competitive_landscape.difference: ProSA measures instance-level performance sensitivity and relates it to decoding confidence; this paper decomposes stochastic output variation into intent, articulation, and residual factors without requiring one correctness target.

competitive_landscape.title: Quantifying Language Models' Sensitivity to Spurious Features in Prompt Design or: How I learned to start worrying about prompt formatting
competitive_landscape.difference: FormatSpread audits accuracy ranges under formatting perturbations; the reviewed method covers semantic paraphrases, repeated distributions, and explicit between-intent separation.

competitive_landscape.title: Evaluating the World Model Implicit in a Generative Model
competitive_landscape.difference: Uses known finite-automaton state equivalence and valid-continuation oracles; the reviewed paper generalizes the invariance/distinction idea to evaluator-defined, stochastic, open-ended intent but loses an intrinsic correctness oracle.

competitive_landscape.title: IntentGrasp: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Intent Understanding
competitive_landscape.difference: Evaluates explicit intent-label prediction across 49 corpora and 12 domains and tests intent-focused fine-tuning; it complements rather than replaces this paper's response-distribution invariance diagnostic.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims a formal evaluator-relative definition of intent comprehension and a scalable variance-decomposition diagnostic for stochastic model responses.
novelty_assessment.evidence: It joins same-intent consistency and different-intent sensitivity, provides numeric/categorical/free-text extensions, validates a large repeated-response pipeline, and reports nested uncertainty estimates.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The joint sensitivity/invariance framing and variance accounting are useful additions to prompt-robustness work. Calling the result comprehension is stronger than the evidence: the metric is a behavioral consistency score whose validity depends on constructed intents, evaluator mappings, and task utility.

reviewer_notes: Read all 50 extracted pages, including categorical and embedding extensions, human audit, REML estimator, correctness variants, temperature/draw-count checks, and full prompt pipeline. Author results are separated from the key reviewer caveat that variance components do not identify internal understanding. Primary arXiv records, including the subsequent IntentGrasp benchmark, were checked on 2026-08-23.
